questions.q: What does “adequate” mean?
o: Good enough for a particular purpose
questions.e: « adequate » veut dire : suffisant, adéquat.

questions.q: What does “assume” mean?
o: Accept something as true without proof
questions.e: « assume » veut dire : supposer, présumer.

questions.q: What does “cease” mean?
o: Stop happening or stop doing something
questions.e: « cease » veut dire : cesser.

questions.q: What does “consume” mean?
questions.e: « consume » veut dire : consommer.

questions.q: What does “contribute” mean?
o: Give or add something to a shared effort
questions.e: « contribute » veut dire : contribuer.

questions.q: What does “crucial” mean?
questions.e: « crucial » veut dire : crucial, essentiel.

questions.q: What does “expose” mean?
o: Make something hidden known or visible
questions.e: « expose » veut dire : révéler, dévoiler.

questions.q: What does “factor” mean in “cost is a factor”?
o: One thing that helps cause a result
questions.e: « factor » veut dire : facteur, élément qui influence.

questions.q: What does “former” mean in “the former teacher”?
o: A person with no such role
The person who had that role before
The person who has the role now
The person who will have the role next
questions.e: « former » veut dire : ancien (qui occupait ce rôle avant).

questions.q: What does “impact” mean?
questions.e: « impact » veut dire : impact, effet.

questions.q: What does “maintain” mean?
o: Keep something in good condition or continue it
questions.e: « maintain » veut dire : entretenir, maintenir.

questions.q: What does “obtain” mean?
questions.e: « obtain » veut dire : obtenir.

questions.q: What does “precise” mean?
questions.e: « precise » veut dire : précis, exact.

questions.q: What does “prevent” mean?
questions.e: « prevent » veut dire : empêcher.

questions.q: What does “pursue” mean?
o: Continue trying to achieve or follow something
questions.e: « pursue » veut dire : poursuivre (un but).

questions.q: What does “require” mean?
questions.e: « require » veut dire : exiger, nécessiter.

questions.q: What does “retain” mean?
o: Keep or continue to have something
questions.e: « retain » veut dire : conserver, garder.

questions.q: What does “shift” mean as a verb?
questions.e: « shift » veut dire : changer, se déplacer légèrement.

questions.q: What does “significant” mean?
o: Important or large enough to matter
questions.e: « significant » veut dire : important, significatif.

questions.q: What does “source” mean?
o: The last step in a process
The place or person something comes from
questions.e: « source » veut dire : source, origine.

questions.q: What does “temporary” mean?
questions.e: « temporary » veut dire : temporaire.

questions.q: What does “valid” mean?
o: Acceptable or supported by good reasons
questions.e: « valid » veut dire : valable, fondé.

questions.q: What does “widespread” mean?
o: Found or happening in many places
questions.e: « widespread » veut dire : répandu.

questions.q: What does “obstacle” mean?
questions.e: « obstacle » veut dire : obstacle.

questions.q: What does “allocate” mean?
o: Assign something for a particular purpose
Borrow something for a short time
questions.e: « allocate » veut dire : attribuer, allouer.

questions.q: What does “anticipate” mean?
questions.e: « anticipate » veut dire : anticiper, prévoir.

questions.q: What does “assess” mean?
o: Evaluate the quality or importance of something
questions.e: « assess » veut dire : évaluer.

questions.q: What is “bias”?
o: An unfair preference for or against someone
questions.e: « bias » veut dire : parti pris, préjugé.

questions.q: What does “coherent” mean?
questions.e: « coherent » veut dire : cohérent.

questions.q: What does “consecutive” mean?
o: Following one after another without a break
questions.e: « consecutive » veut dire : consécutif.

questions.q: What does “controversial” mean?
questions.e: « controversial » veut dire : controversé.

questions.q: What does “derive” mean?
questions.e: « derive » veut dire : tirer de, provenir de.

questions.q: What does “distort” mean?
o: Change something so it is no longer accurate
questions.e: « distort » veut dire : déformer.

questions.q: What does “enhance” mean?
o: Improve the quality or value of something
questions.e: « enhance » veut dire : améliorer, renforcer.

questions.q: What does “ethical” mean?
o: Related to principles of right and wrong
questions.e: « ethical » veut dire : éthique, moral.

questions.q: What does “fundamental” mean?
questions.e: « fundamental » veut dire : fondamental.

questions.q: What does “implement” mean as a verb?
o: Put a plan or decision into effect
Change the meaning of a word
questions.e: « implement » veut dire : mettre en œuvre.

questions.q: What does “infer” mean?
questions.e: « infer » veut dire : déduire.

questions.q: What is “integrity”?
questions.e: « integrity » veut dire : intégrité.

questions.q: What does “justify” mean?
o: Give a good reason for an action or claim
questions.e: « justify » veut dire : justifier.

questions.q: What is a “mechanism”?
o: A system or process that makes something work
questions.e: « mechanism » veut dire : mécanisme.

questions.q: What is a “notion”?
questions.e: « notion » veut dire : notion, idée.

questions.q: What does “offset” mean?
o: Move something to a new place
Counterbalance or reduce the effect of something
questions.e: « offset » veut dire : compenser.

questions.q: What does “predominant” mean?
questions.e: « predominant » veut dire : prédominant.

questions.q: What does “refine” mean?
questions.e: « refine » veut dire : affiner, perfectionner.

questions.q: What does “regulate” mean?
questions.e: « regulate » veut dire : réglementer, contrôler.

questions.q: What does “substantial” mean?
questions.e: « substantial » veut dire : considérable, important.

questions.q: What does “undergo” mean?
o: Experience or be subjected to a process
questions.e: « undergo » veut dire : subir, connaître (un changement).

questions.q: What is the French for “scarce”?

questions.q: What is the French for “evidence”?
questions.e: « evidence » se traduit par « preuve ».

questions.q: What is the French for “outcome”?
questions.e: « outcome » se traduit par « résultat ».

questions.q: What is the French for “to assess”?
questions.e: « to assess » se traduit par « évaluer ».

questions.q: What is the French for “aware”?
questions.e: « aware » se traduit par « conscient ».

questions.q: What is the French for “issue” in “a social issue”?
questions.e: « issue » se traduit par « problème ».

questions.q: What is the French for “approach” mean as a noun?
questions.e: « approach » se traduit par « méthode ».

questions.q: What is the French for “to enhance”?
questions.e: « to enhance » se traduit par « améliorer ».

questions.q: What is the French for “drawback”?
questions.e: « drawback » se traduit par « inconvénient ».

questions.q: What is the French for “to maintain”?
questions.e: « to maintain » se traduit par « maintenir ».

questions.q: What is the French for “eventually”?
questions.e: « eventually » se traduit par « finalement ».

questions.q: What is the French for “accurate”?
questions.e: « accurate » se traduit par « exact ».

questions.q: What is the French for “to prohibit”?
questions.e: « to prohibit » se traduit par « interdire ».

questions.q: What is the French for “significant”?
questions.e: « significant » se traduit par « important ».

questions.q: What is the French for “to undergo”?
questions.e: « to undergo » se traduit par « subir ».

questions.q: What is the French for “awareness”?
questions.e: « awareness » se traduit par « sensibilisation ».

questions.q: What is the French for “sustainable”?
questions.e: « sustainable » se traduit par « durable ».

questions.q: What is the French for “regardless”?
questions.e: « regardless » se traduit par « sans tenir compte de ».

questions.q: What is the French for “to advocate”?
questions.e: « to advocate » se traduit par « défendre une cause ».

questions.q: What is the French for “widespread”?
questions.e: « widespread » se traduit par « répandu ».

questions.q: What is the French for “to allocate”?
questions.e: « to allocate » se traduit par « attribuer ».

questions.q: What is the French for “consequence”?
questions.e: « consequence » se traduit par « conséquence ».

questions.q: What is the French for “feasible”?
questions.e: « feasible » se traduit par « réalisable ».

questions.q: What is the French for “reluctant”?
questions.e: « reluctant » se traduit par « réticent ».

questions.q: The new policy will be implemented next month. What does implemented mean?
questions.e: Implement veut dire mettre en œuvre.

questions.q: The plan is feasible with the available tools. What does feasible mean?
questions.e: Feasible veut dire réalisable.

questions.q: The measurements must be accurate. What does accurate mean?
questions.e: Accurate veut dire exact et précis.

questions.q: The storm had a serious impact on transport. What does impact mean?
questions.e: Impact veut dire effet ou conséquence.

questions.q: She was reluctant to change the schedule. What does reluctant mean?
questions.e: Reluctant veut dire peu disposé.

questions.q: Fresh water is scarce in the region. What does scarce mean?
questions.e: Scarce veut dire rare ou en quantité limitée.

questions.q: A new problem emerged during the meeting. What does emerged mean?
questions.e: Emerge veut dire apparaître.

questions.q: The archive retains copies of each letter. What does retains mean?
questions.e: Retain veut dire garder.

questions.q: The council allocated funds to the clinics. What does allocated mean?
questions.e: Allocate veut dire répartir ou attribuer pour un usage.

questions.q: The outcome surprised the researchers. What does outcome mean?
questions.e: Outcome veut dire résultat.

questions.q: The new rules require all visitors to register. What does require mean?
questions.e: Require veut dire exiger, rendre nécessaire.

questions.q: The exercise was beneficial to the learners. What does beneficial mean?
questions.e: Beneficial veut dire bénéfique, qui aide.

questions.q: The team collected evidence before making a claim. What does evidence mean?
questions.e: Evidence veut dire preuve ou élément qui appuie une idée.

questions.q: The committee conducted interviews with families. What does conducted mean?
questions.e: Conduct veut dire mener ou effectuer une activité.

questions.q: The number of errors declined after practice. What does declined mean?
questions.e: Decline veut dire diminuer.

questions.q: Her account is consistent with the written record. What does consistent mean?
questions.e: Consistent with veut dire en accord avec.

questions.q: The discovery was significant for local history. What does significant mean?
questions.e: Significant veut dire important.

questions.q: Readers must interpret the chart carefully. What does interpret mean?
questions.e: Interpret veut dire interpréter, expliquer le sens.

questions.q: A lack of transport is a major constraint. What does constraint mean?
questions.e: Constraint veut dire limite ou contrainte.

questions.q: The school will evaluate the new programme. What does evaluate mean?
questions.e: Evaluate veut dire évaluer, juger le résultat.

questions.q: Do not assume the message is true. What does assume mean?
questions.e: Assume veut dire supposer, croire sans preuve.

questions.q: The first route is shorter, whereas the second is safer. What does whereas mean?
questions.e: Whereas sert à opposer deux faits.

questions.q: Eventually, the rain stopped. What does eventually mean?
questions.e: Eventually veut dire finalement, après un certain temps.

questions.q: Despite the delay, the lesson continued. What does despite mean?
questions.e: Despite veut dire malgré.

questions.q: To ___ is to leave your own country in order to live permanently in another one.
questions.e: Emigrate = quitter son pays (émigrer). Immigrate = s'installer dans un nouveau pays (immigrer).

questions.q: The money that migrants send to their families back home is called ___.
questions.e: Remittances = transferts d'argent des migrants vers leur pays d'origine.

questions.q: The departure of highly qualified doctors and engineers to richer countries is known as the ___.
questions.e: Brain drain = fuite des cerveaux.

questions.q: A person forced to flee their country because of war or persecution is a ___.
questions.e: Refugee = réfugié, personne qui fuit la guerre ou la persécution.

questions.q: The Senegalese ___ in France, Italy and the USA contributes greatly to the national economy.
questions.e: Diaspora = ensemble des membres d'un peuple vivant hors de leur pays.

questions.q: A person who organizes dangerous sea crossings in exchange for money is a ___.
questions.e: Smuggler = passeur, contrebandier. Coastguard = garde-côte.

questions.q: The country that receives migrants is called the ___ country.
questions.e: Host country = pays d'accueil. Home country = pays d'origine.

questions.q: The slogan « Barça ou Barsakh » shows that some young people were ready to ___ their lives to reach Europe.
questions.e: Risk one's life = risquer sa vie.

questions.q: To ___ into a new society means to become part of it while adapting to its way of life.
questions.e: Integrate = s'intégrer. Segregate = séparer, ségréguer.

questions.q: A person who travels every day between home and work, for example from Thiès to Dakar, is a ___.
questions.e: Commuter = navetteur, personne qui fait le trajet domicile-travail chaque jour.

questions.q: A person who asks a foreign government for protection is called an ___ seeker.
questions.e: Asylum seeker = demandeur d'asile.

questions.q: People who move because of drought, floods or rising sea levels are part of ___ migration.
questions.e: Climate migration = migration climatique.

questions.q: A student who leaves school before finishing their studies is a ___.
questions.e: Dropout = élève en décrochage scolaire. Graduate = diplômé.

questions.q: The ability to read and write is called ___.
questions.e: Literacy = alphabétisation, capacité à lire et écrire. Literature = littérature.

questions.q: In many countries, education is ___ until the age of 16: all children must go to school.
questions.e: Compulsory = obligatoire. Optional = facultatif.

questions.q: She won a ___ to study agronomy at UGB, so she will not pay any tuition fees.
questions.e: Scholarship = bourse d'études.

questions.q: Training that prepares young people for a specific trade, such as plumbing or sewing, is called ___ training.
questions.e: Vocational training = formation professionnelle.

questions.q: To ___ at a university means to register officially as a student there.
questions.e: Enrol = s'inscrire. Expel = renvoyer.

questions.q: A person who has completed a university degree is a ___.
questions.e: Graduate = diplômé (de l'université).

questions.q: The ___ is the set of subjects and contents taught in a school system.
questions.e: Curriculum = programme scolaire.

questions.q: The money that students pay to a private school or university is called tuition ___.
questions.e: Tuition fees = frais de scolarité.

questions.q: He was ___ from school for cheating during the exam.
questions.e: Expel = exclure, renvoyer d'un établissement.

questions.q: The cutting down of forests on a large scale is called ___.
questions.e: Deforestation = déforestation. Reforestation = reboisement.

questions.q: The process by which fertile land slowly becomes desert is called ___.
questions.e: Desertification = désertification.

questions.q: In Saint-Louis, the sea is slowly eating away the Langue de Barbarie. This is coastal ___.
questions.e: Coastal erosion = érosion côtière.

questions.q: Solar and wind power are ___ sources of energy because they never run out.
questions.e: Renewable = renouvelable. Fossil fuels = combustibles fossiles.

questions.q: Carbon dioxide is a ___ gas that contributes to global warming.
questions.e: Greenhouse gas = gaz à effet de serre.

questions.q: Catching fish faster than they can reproduce is called ___.
questions.e: Overfishing = surpêche, un grand problème pour les pêcheurs de Kayar et de Joal.

questions.q: The variety of plants and animals living in a region is called ___.
questions.e: Biodiversity = biodiversité. Biology = la science du vivant.

questions.q: The Great Green Wall is a project to plant trees across the Sahel in order to ___ the advance of the desert.
questions.e: Halt = stopper, arrêter.

questions.q: Plastic waste is a serious ___ to marine life.
questions.e: Threat = menace. Treat = traiter, thread = fil, throat = gorge.

questions.q: To ___ the effects of climate change means to make them less severe.
questions.e: Mitigate = atténuer. Aggravate = aggraver.

questions.q: Burning more fossil fuels will only ___ the problem of global warming.
questions.e: Exacerbate = aggraver, exacerber.

questions.q: Farmers in the Sahel must become more ___ in order to survive long droughts.
questions.e: Resilient = résilient, capable de résister et de se relever.

questions.q: Low-lying coastal cities are particularly ___ to rising sea levels.
questions.e: Vulnerable to = vulnérable, exposé à.

questions.q: Our ecological ___ measures how much of nature's resources we use.
questions.e: Ecological footprint = empreinte écologique.

questions.q: The percentage of registered voters who actually vote is called the voter ___.
questions.e: Turnout = taux de participation. Turnover = chiffre d'affaires ou rotation du personnel.

questions.q: Voters put their ___ in the box at the polling station.
questions.e: Ballot = bulletin de vote. Bullet = balle (d'arme).

questions.q: Leaders should be ___: they must explain their decisions and answer for them.
questions.e: Accountable = responsable, qui rend des comptes.

questions.q: Offering money to an official to obtain an unfair advantage is called ___.
questions.e: Bribery = corruption (verser un pot-de-vin). Bribe = pot-de-vin.

questions.q: An official who secretly takes public money that was placed in his care ___ it.
questions.e: Embezzle = détourner des fonds.

questions.q: A ___ is an official count of the population of a country.
questions.e: Census = recensement.

questions.q: After long discussions, the members of the assembly finally reached a ___.
questions.e: Reach a consensus = parvenir à un consensus, un accord général.

questions.q: A state that governs itself without control from outside has full ___.
questions.e: Sovereignty = souveraineté.

questions.q: Senegal gained its ___ from France in 1960.
questions.e: Independence = indépendance (4 avril 1960 pour le Sénégal).

questions.q: In a ___ election, voters choose the head of state.
questions.e: Presidential = présidentiel (adjectif).

questions.q: A judge must be ___: she must not favour either side.
questions.e: Impartial = impartial, neutre. Biased = partial, qui a un parti pris.

questions.q: In a ___, citizens choose their leaders through free and fair elections.
questions.e: Democracy = démocratie.

questions.q: Freedom of ___ is the right to express your opinions publicly.
questions.e: Freedom of speech = liberté d'expression.

questions.q: When registered citizens choose not to vote, it is called ___.
questions.e: Abstention = abstention.

questions.q: Programmes that give women more control over their own lives and choices promote women's ___.
questions.e: Empowerment = autonomisation, renforcement du pouvoir d'agir.

questions.q: Treating someone unfairly because of their sex, religion or ethnic group is ___.
questions.e: Discrimination = discrimination.

questions.q: The idea that « girls are not good at maths » is a ___.
questions.e: Stereotype = stéréotype, idée reçue.

questions.q: Senegal's ___ law requires equal numbers of men and women on electoral lists.
questions.e: Parity = parité. La loi sur la parité a été adoptée au Sénégal en 2010.

questions.q: Marrying a girl before the age of 18 is called child or early ___.
questions.e: Early marriage = mariage précoce.

questions.q: When prices keep rising and money buys less and less, there is ___.
questions.e: Inflation = inflation, hausse générale des prix.

questions.q: Small loans given to people who cannot borrow from ordinary banks are called ___.
questions.e: Microcredit = microcrédit.

questions.q: Street vendors and small unregistered workshops belong to the ___ sector.
questions.e: Informal sector = secteur informel.

questions.q: A person who starts and runs their own business is an ___.
questions.e: Entrepreneur = entrepreneur, créateur d'entreprise.

questions.q: The government pays a ___ to keep the price of rice low for consumers.
questions.e: Subsidy = subvention.

questions.q: The money a person receives regularly from work or investments is their ___.
questions.e: Income = revenu. Expense = dépense.

questions.q: Many young graduates cannot find jobs: youth ___ is high.
questions.e: Unemployment = chômage.

questions.q: When a country's economy shrinks for several months in a row, it is in ___.
questions.e: Recession = récession. Expansion = croissance.

questions.q: Many families live in ___: they cannot meet their basic needs.
questions.e: Poverty = pauvreté. Prosperity = prospérité, property = propriété.

questions.q: A disease that spreads quickly to many people in one region is an ___.
questions.e: Epidemic = épidémie.

questions.q: COVID-19 was a ___ because it spread all over the world.
questions.e: Pandemic = pandémie, épidémie mondiale.

questions.q: Not eating the right kinds of food leads to ___.
questions.e: Malnutrition = malnutrition.

questions.q: Clean toilets, drains and the safe disposal of waste are part of good ___.
questions.e: Sanitation = assainissement.

questions.q: Life ___ is the average number of years that people live.
questions.e: Life expectancy = espérance de vie.

questions.q: A sudden start of a disease such as cholera in a town is called an ___.
questions.e: Outbreak = flambée, apparition soudaine d'une maladie.

questions.q: The gap between people who have access to the internet and those who do not is the digital ___.
questions.e: Digital divide = fracture numérique.

questions.q: Crimes committed with computers and the internet are called ___.
questions.e: Cybercrime = cybercriminalité.

questions.q: Spending too many hours on social media can lead to ___.
questions.e: Addiction = dépendance, addiction. Addition = addition (calcul).

questions.q: Apps that collect your personal data can threaten your ___.
questions.e: Privacy = vie privée.

questions.q: The growing connection between the economies and cultures of the world is called ___.
questions.e: Globalization = mondialisation.

questions.q: The traditions, monuments and values passed down from earlier generations form our cultural ___.
questions.e: Cultural heritage = patrimoine culturel.

questions.q: In West Africa, griots transmitted history through ___ tradition.
questions.e: Oral tradition = tradition orale.

questions.q: Négritude was a literary and political ___ led by Senghor, Césaire and Damas.
questions.e: Movement = mouvement.

questions.q: When a colonized people is pushed to adopt the colonizer's culture and lose its own, it is called ___.
questions.e: Assimilation = assimilation (politique coloniale française).

questions.q: The feeling of being a stranger in your own culture or society is ___.
questions.e: Alienation = aliénation.

questions.q: « The test was a piece of cake. » This means the test was ___.
questions.e: A piece of cake = très facile (« du gâteau »).

questions.q: « I'm feeling a bit under the weather today. » This means ___.
questions.e: Under the weather = un peu malade, patraque.

questions.q: « This new phone costs an arm and a leg. » This means it is ___.
questions.e: Cost an arm and a leg = coûter les yeux de la tête.

questions.q: « I see my cousins in Canada once in a blue moon. » This means I see them ___.
questions.e: Once in a blue moon = très rarement.

questions.q: « You've hit the nail on the head! » This means ___.
questions.e: Hit the nail on the head = mettre le doigt dessus, viser juste.

questions.q: Before the BAC, many students « burn the midnight oil ». This means they ___.
questions.e: Burn the midnight oil = travailler tard dans la nuit.

questions.q: At the start of the workshop, the facilitator told a joke to « break the ice ». This means to ___.
questions.e: Break the ice = briser la glace, détendre l'atmosphère.

questions.q: « He let the cat out of the bag. » This means he ___.
questions.e: Let the cat out of the bag = vendre la mèche.

questions.q: « His rude comment was the last straw. » This means it was ___.
o: the final problem that made someone lose patience
questions.e: The last straw = la goutte d'eau qui fait déborder le vase.

questions.q: « My brother and I don't see eye to eye on politics. » This means we ___.
questions.e: Not see eye to eye = ne pas être d'accord.

questions.q: « It's 7 p.m. Let's call it a day. » This means ___.
o: let's give this day a name
questions.e: Call it a day = s'arrêter là pour aujourd'hui.

questions.q: « Stop pulling my leg! » This means ___.
questions.e: Pull someone's leg = faire marcher quelqu'un, plaisanter.

questions.q: « He got cold feet the day before his speech. » This means he ___.
o: became too nervous and nearly gave up
questions.e: Get cold feet = avoir la trouille, hésiter au dernier moment.

questions.q: « Keep an eye on the pot of rice while I go out. » This means ___.
questions.e: Keep an eye on = surveiller.

questions.q: « Don't bite off more than you can chew. » This means ___.
o: don't take on more than you can manage
don't talk with food in your mouth
questions.e: Bite off more than you can chew = avoir les yeux plus gros que le ventre, trop en entreprendre.

questions.q: « She's in hot water with her boss. » This means she is ___.
questions.e: Be in hot water = être dans le pétrin.

questions.q: « Actions speak louder than words. » This means ___.
o: what you do matters more than what you say
questions.e: Les actes comptent plus que les paroles.

questions.q: « Every cloud has a silver lining. » This means ___.
o: something good can come from a bad situation
questions.e: À quelque chose malheur est bon.

questions.q: « Better late than never. » This means ___.
o: it is better to do something late than not at all
questions.e: Mieux vaut tard que jamais.

questions.q: « Before we start, let's make sure we're all on the same page. » This means ___.
o: let's make sure we understand things the same way
let's sit in the same row
questions.e: Be on the same page = être sur la même longueur d'onde.

questions.q: The researchers will ___ a survey in ten villages around Kébémer.
questions.e: Carry out = mener, réaliser (une enquête, une expérience).

questions.q: The meeting has been ___ until next week because of the heavy rain.
questions.e: Put off = reporter, remettre à plus tard.

questions.q: The match was ___ because of the storm; it will not take place at all.
questions.e: Call off = annuler.

questions.q: She ___ a brilliant idea to collect plastic waste in her neighbourhood.
questions.e: Come up with = trouver, imaginer (une idée).

questions.q: Many young people ___ their older brothers and sisters and want to be like them.
questions.e: Look up to = admirer. Look down on = mépriser.

questions.q: It is hard to ___ the extreme heat in Matam in May.
questions.e: Cope with = faire face à, supporter.

questions.q: My grandmother ___ eight children on her own.
questions.e: Bring up = élever (des enfants).

questions.q: Two friends from Louga ___ a small company that makes mobile apps.
questions.e: Set up = créer, fonder (une entreprise).

questions.q: The company ___ my job application because I had no experience.
questions.e: Turn down = refuser, rejeter.

questions.q: A fire ___ in the market during the night.
questions.e: Break out = éclater, se déclarer (incendie, guerre, épidémie).

questions.q: The police are ___ the causes of the accident on the national road.
questions.e: Look into = enquêter sur, examiner.

questions.q: After the blood test, the doctor ___ malaria: the patient has typhoid.
questions.e: Rule out = écarter, exclure (une possibilité).

questions.q: The teacher ___ that several answers were missing from my essay.
questions.e: Point out = faire remarquer, signaler.

questions.q: After weeks of pressure from the strikers, the company finally ___ and raised salaries.
questions.e: Give in = céder.

questions.q: I can't ___ this noise any longer!
questions.e: Put up with = supporter, tolérer.

questions.q: He was ill for three weeks and ___ with his schoolwork.
questions.e: Fall behind = prendre du retard.

questions.q: She ___ of school at 15 to help her mother at the market.
questions.e: Drop out of school = abandonner l'école.

questions.q: We must ___ plastic bags; they pollute our fields and kill our animals.
questions.e: Get rid of = se débarrasser de.

questions.q: Agriculture ___ a large share of jobs in rural Senegal.
questions.e: Account for = représenter (une proportion).

questions.q: He worked on Saturday to ___ the time he had lost during the week.
questions.e: Make up for = compenser, rattraper.

questions.q: You can always ___ me; I'll help you whenever you need it.
questions.e: Count on = compter sur.

questions.q: It took her months to ___ the death of her grandfather.
questions.e: Get over = se remettre de.

questions.q: The old fishing rules will be ___ gradually over five years and replaced by new ones.
questions.e: Phase out = supprimer progressivement.

questions.q: Her daughter really ___ her: same smile, same voice.
questions.e: Take after = ressembler à (un parent).

questions.q: When the director retired, his deputy ___ the company.
questions.e: Take over = prendre la direction, reprendre.

questions.q: The English word « actually » means ___.
questions.e: Faux ami : actually = en fait. Actuellement = currently, at present.

questions.q: A « sensible » person in English is someone who is ___.
questions.e: Faux ami : sensible = raisonnable. « Sensible » en français = sensitive.

questions.q: « I attended the conference in Dakar. » This means I ___.
questions.e: Faux ami : attend = assister à. Attendre = wait for.

questions.q: In a university, a « lecture » is ___.
o: a talk given to students on a subject
questions.e: Faux ami : lecture = cours magistral, conférence. La lecture = reading.

questions.q: « She achieved her goal. » This means she ___.
questions.e: Faux ami : achieve = atteindre, réaliser (et non « achever » = finish).

questions.q: « The deception hurt her deeply. » Here « deception » means ___.
questions.e: Faux ami : deception = tromperie. Déception = disappointment.

questions.q: « I need to assist my father in the shop. » This means I need to ___ my father.
questions.e: Faux ami : assist = aider. Assister à = attend.

questions.q: How do you say « formation professionnelle » in English?
questions.e: Formation (éducation) = training. Formation professionnelle = vocational training.

questions.q: « She is very sympathetic. » This means she ___.
o: shows understanding for people who suffer
questions.e: Faux ami : sympathetic = compatissant. Sympathique = nice, friendly.

questions.q: « Classes will resume on Monday. » Here « resume » means ___.
questions.e: Faux ami : resume = reprendre. Résumer = summarize.

questions.q: « The rent was too high, so they moved. » Here « rent » means ___.
o: the money paid to live in a house
questions.e: Faux ami : rent = loyer. Une rente = an annuity, a private income.

questions.q: « The location of the new school is ideal. » Here « location » means ___.
questions.e: Faux ami : location = emplacement. Une location = a rental.

questions.q: « Two passengers were injured in the accident. » Here « injured » means ___.
questions.e: Faux ami : injure = blesser. Injurier = insult.

questions.q: The farmers worked very hard; ___, the harvest was poor because of the drought.
questions.e: However = cependant (opposition).

questions.q: There was no rain for months; ___, many animals died.
questions.e: Consequently = par conséquent (conséquence).

questions.q: ___ she was very tired, she finished her homework.
questions.e: Although + proposition = bien que. Despite + nom ou -ing.

questions.q: Education is a basic right. ___, it is the key to development.
questions.e: Moreover = de plus (addition).

questions.q: You will fail the exam ___ you study more.
questions.e: Unless = à moins que, sauf si.

questions.q: Hurry up, ___ you will miss the last bus to Kébémer.
questions.e: Otherwise = sinon.

questions.q: The flight to Ziguinchor was cancelled ___ bad weather.
questions.e: Owing to + nom = en raison de.

questions.q: You can borrow my laptop ___ you give it back tomorrow.
questions.e: As long as = à condition que.

questions.q: The road was flooded. ___, we arrived on time.
questions.e: Nevertheless = néanmoins, pourtant.

questions.q: She studies hard ___ she can win a scholarship.
questions.e: So that = afin que, pour que (but).

questions.q: The project failed ___ a lack of funding.
questions.e: Due to + nom = à cause de, en raison de.

questions.q: What is the noun of « perceive »?
questions.e: Perceive → perception. Perceptive est un adjectif.

questions.q: What is the noun of « deny »?
questions.e: Deny → denial (le déni, le refus).

questions.q: What is the noun of « analyse »?
questions.e: Analyse → analysis (pluriel : analyses).

questions.q: To make something stronger is to ___ it.
questions.e: Le suffixe -en forme des verbes : strengthen, widen, shorten.

questions.q: What is the opposite of « legal »?
questions.e: Devant un l, le préfixe négatif est il- : illegal, illiterate.

questions.q: A person who cannot read or write is ___.
questions.e: Illiterate = analphabète. Literate = alphabétisé.

questions.q: What is the noun of « responsible »?
questions.e: Responsible → responsibility (la responsabilité). Responsiveness = réactivité.

questions.q: What is the adjective related to « poverty »?
questions.e: Poverty (la pauvreté) → poor (pauvre).

questions.q: What is the noun of « corrupt »?
questions.e: Corrupt → corruption.

questions.q: To make a road wider is to ___ it.
questions.e: Wide → widen (élargir).

questions.q: Which noun refers to the way a state or an organization is managed?
questions.e: Governance = gouvernance.

questions.q: Someone who is not mature is ___.
questions.e: Mature → immature.

questions.q: What is the noun of « able »?
questions.e: Able → ability (la capacité).

questions.q: To make a town or a system more modern is to ___ it.
questions.e: Modern → modernize (moderniser).

questions.q: What is the noun of « vary »?
questions.e: Vary → variety (la variété). Attention à l'orthographe : variation, et non varyation.

questions.q: What is the noun of « fail »?
questions.e: Fail → failure (l'échec).

questions.q: The campaign aims to ___ awareness about malaria.
questions.e: Raise awareness = sensibiliser.

questions.q: The government must ___ measures to reduce road accidents.
questions.e: Take measures = prendre des mesures.

questions.q: Plastic pollution ___ a serious threat to our oceans.
questions.e: Pose a threat = constituer une menace.

questions.q: Women ___ a key role in the local economy of Kébémer.
questions.e: Play a role = jouer un rôle.

questions.q: Before you ___ conclusions, read all the evidence.
questions.e: Draw conclusions = tirer des conclusions.

questions.q: Scientists at ISRA ___ research on drought-resistant millet.
questions.e: Conduct research = mener des recherches.

questions.q: When you plan the budget, you must take every expense into ___.
questions.e: Take into account = prendre en compte.

questions.q: ___ in mind that the exam starts at 8 a.m. sharp.
questions.e: Bear in mind = garder à l'esprit.

questions.q: The new minister promised to ___ the issue of youth unemployment.
questions.e: Address an issue = s'attaquer à un problème.

questions.q: He was arrested for ___ a crime.
questions.e: Commit a crime = commettre un crime.

questions.q: It is not easy to ___ a balance between work and family life.
questions.e: Strike a balance = trouver un équilibre.

questions.q: Our country is ___ progress in reducing illiteracy.
questions.e: Make progress = faire des progrès.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to « abundant »?
questions.e: Abundant = plentiful = abondant.

questions.q: « Small businesses thrive in this neighbourhood. » Here « thrive » means ___.
questions.e: Thrive = prospérer.

questions.q: « The patient's health deteriorated during the night. » Here « deteriorated » means ___.
questions.e: Deteriorate = se détériorer, empirer.

questions.q: « The question was ambiguous. » This means it ___.
o: could be understood in more than one way
questions.e: Ambiguous = ambigu.

questions.q: « Typewriters are now obsolete. » This means they are ___.
questions.e: Obsolete = obsolète, dépassé.

questions.q: « The two groups were hostile to each other. » Here « hostile » means ___.
questions.e: Hostile = hostile.

questions.q: « Change is inevitable. » This means change ___.
questions.e: Inevitable = inévitable.

questions.q: A « prosperous » town is a town that is ___.
questions.e: Prosperous = prospère.

questions.q: A « diligent » student is one who ___.
o: works carefully and with great effort
questions.e: Diligent = appliqué, assidu.

questions.q: « She checked every detail; she is meticulous. » Here « meticulous » means ___.
questions.e: Meticulous = méticuleux.

questions.q: An « eloquent » speaker is someone who ___.
questions.e: Eloquent = éloquent.

questions.q: « Copying the same sentence a hundred times is tedious. » Here « tedious » means ___.
questions.e: Tedious = fastidieux, ennuyeux.

questions.q: « Don't waste time on such trivial matters. » Here « trivial » means ___.
questions.e: Trivial = insignifiant, sans importance.

questions.q: « Mobile phones are ubiquitous in Dakar. » This means they are ___.
questions.e: Ubiquitous = omniprésent.

questions.q: « The minister was compelled to resign. » Here « compelled » means ___.
questions.e: Be compelled to = être contraint de.

questions.q: « The authorities banned plastic bags. » Here « banned » means ___.
questions.e: Ban = interdire officiellement.

questions.q: « Her argument was convincing. » This means it ___.
questions.e: Convincing = convaincant.

questions.q: « The rain was incessant. » This means the rain ___.
questions.e: Incessant = incessant, continuel.

questions.q: A « tentative » plan is a plan that is ___.
questions.e: Faux ami : tentative = provisoire, hésitant. Une tentative = an attempt.

questions.q: « The village is very remote. » This means it is ___.
o: far away from towns and cities
questions.e: Remote = isolé, éloigné.

questions.q: An « inhabitant » of Kébémer is ___.
o: a person who lives in Kébémer
questions.e: Inhabitant = habitant.

questions.q: The word « urban » refers to ___.
questions.e: Urban = urbain. Rural = rural.

questions.q: The « rural exodus » refers to ___.
o: people leaving the countryside for the cities
questions.e: Rural exodus = exode rural.

questions.q: A « thorough » investigation is one that is ___.
questions.e: Thorough = minutieux, approfondi.

questions.q: « Kayar relies on fishing. » Here « relies on » means ___.
questions.e: Rely on = dépendre de, compter sur.

questions.q: « The negotiations were fruitful. » This means they ___.
questions.e: Fruitful = fructueux.

questions.q: To « foster » cooperation between schools means to ___ it.
questions.e: Foster = favoriser, encourager.

questions.q: To « hinder » progress means to ___ it.
o: slow it down or block it
questions.e: Hinder = freiner, entraver.

questions.q: To « boost » the economy means to ___ it.
questions.e: Boost = stimuler, relancer.

questions.q: To « tackle » a problem means to ___.
questions.e: Tackle a problem = s'attaquer à un problème.

questions.q: To « curb » corruption means to ___ it.
questions.e: Curb = freiner, limiter.

questions.q: « The floods displaced thousands of people. » Here « displaced » means ___.
o: forced them to leave their homes
questions.e: Displace = déplacer de force. Displaced persons = personnes déplacées.

questions.q: A « plea » for help is ___.
questions.e: Plea = appel, supplication.

questions.q: To « overcome » obstacles means to ___.
questions.e: Overcome = surmonter.

questions.q: « Gender equality » means ___.
o: equal rights and opportunities for women and men
the same salary for every job
separate schools for boys and girls
questions.e: Gender equality = égalité entre les femmes et les hommes.

questions.q: An « outstanding » student is ___.
questions.e: Outstanding = remarquable, exceptionnel.

questions.q: A « breakthrough » in medicine is ___.
questions.e: Breakthrough = percée, avancée majeure.

questions.q: « The council's decision was unanimous. » This means ___.
questions.e: Unanimous = unanime.

questions.q: « Hospitality », which Senegalese people call teranga, means ___.
o: being welcoming and generous to guests
questions.e: Hospitality = hospitalité, la teranga.

questions.q: Our « ancestors » are ___.
o: family members who lived long before us
questions.e: Ancestors = ancêtres.

questions.q: « Self-reliance » means ___.
o: depending on yourself rather than on others
questions.e: Self-reliance = autonomie, le fait de compter sur soi-même.

questions.q: « Her commitment to the English Club is impressive. » Here « commitment » means ___.
questions.e: Commitment = engagement, dévouement.

questions.q: What does the idiom "a wolf in sheep's clothing" mean?
o: Someone who seems harmless but is actually dangerous
questions.e: « A wolf in sheep's clothing » désigne une personne dangereuse qui semble inoffensive.

questions.q: What does the idiom "beat a dead horse" mean?
o: To train a horse for racing
To discuss something new and important
To keep discussing something that is already finished or decided
questions.e: « Beat a dead horse » veut dire insister inutilement sur un sujet déjà clos.

questions.q: What does the idiom "burn bridges" mean?
o: To destroy relationships in a way that cannot be repaired
questions.e: « Burn bridges » veut dire couper définitivement les ponts avec quelqu'un.

questions.q: What does the idiom "cut the mustard" mean?
o: To meet the required standard or expectations
questions.e: « Cut the mustard » veut dire être à la hauteur des attentes.

questions.q: What does the idiom "dark horse" mean?
questions.e: Un « dark horse » est un concurrent qui réussit contre toute attente.

questions.q: What does the idiom "drop the ball" mean?
o: To pass responsibility to someone else fairly
To fail to do something properly that you were responsible for
questions.e: « Drop the ball » veut dire échouer dans une tâche dont on était responsable.

questions.q: What does the idiom "every dog has its day" mean?
o: Everyone gets a moment of success or luck eventually
questions.e: Cette expression veut dire que chacun connaît son heure de gloire.

questions.q: What does the idiom "foot the bill" mean?
o: To pay for something, especially an expensive cost
questions.e: « Foot the bill » veut dire payer la facture.

questions.q: What does the idiom "get your ducks in a row" mean?
o: To organise things properly before starting something
questions.e: « Get your ducks in a row » veut dire bien s'organiser avant d'agir.

questions.q: What does the idiom "give someone a run for their money" mean?
o: To easily defeat someone without effort
To provide strong competition for someone
questions.e: « Give someone a run for their money » veut dire représenter une sérieuse concurrence.

questions.q: What does the idiom "go cold turkey" mean?
o: To stop a habit suddenly and completely
questions.e: « Go cold turkey » veut dire arrêter une habitude brusquement.

questions.q: What does the idiom "have an axe to grind" mean?
o: To have a personal reason for disagreeing or complaining about something
To have no opinion at all
questions.e: « Have an axe to grind » veut dire avoir un grief personnel à exprimer.

questions.q: What does the idiom "keep someone at arm's length" mean?
o: To avoid becoming too close or familiar with someone
To become very close friends quickly
questions.e: « Keep someone at arm's length » veut dire garder ses distances avec quelqu'un.

questions.q: What does the idiom "leave no stone unturned" mean?
o: To try every possible method to achieve something
To give up after one attempt
questions.e: « Leave no stone unturned » veut dire tout essayer pour réussir.

questions.q: What does the idiom "let the chips fall where they may" mean?
o: To let events happen naturally without trying to control the outcome
questions.e: « Let the chips fall where they may » veut dire laisser les choses se dérouler naturellement.

questions.q: What does the idiom "make headway" mean?
o: To make progress, especially after difficulty
To go backwards in a project
questions.e: « Make headway » veut dire progresser, notamment après des difficultés.

questions.q: What does the idiom "nip something in the bud" mean?
o: To ignore an early warning sign
To let a problem grow out of control
To cut flowers for a bouquet
To stop a problem early, before it grows worse
questions.e: « Nip something in the bud » veut dire arrêter un problème dès le début.

questions.q: What does the idiom "hear something on the grapevine" mean?
o: To hear information through informal, unofficial channels
questions.e: « Hear it on the grapevine » veut dire apprendre une information par des rumeurs.

questions.q: What does the idiom "par for the course" mean?
o: Something typical or expected in a particular situation
A type of golf score only
questions.e: « Par for the course » veut dire quelque chose de normal, prévisible dans ce contexte.

questions.q: What does the idiom "pay through the nose" mean?
o: To pay an excessively high price for something
questions.e: « Pay through the nose » veut dire payer un prix exagérément élevé.

questions.q: What does the idiom "pull the wool over someone's eyes" mean?
o: To give someone a warm blanket
To tell someone the complete truth
questions.e: « Pull the wool over someone's eyes » veut dire tromper quelqu'un.

questions.q: What does the idiom "put the cart before the horse" mean?
o: To do things in the wrong order
To travel by horse and cart
To correctly follow a logical sequence
questions.e: « Put the cart before the horse » veut dire faire les choses dans le mauvais ordre.

questions.q: What does the idiom "rub someone the wrong way" mean?
o: To give someone a relaxing massage
To irritate or annoy someone, often unintentionally
questions.e: « Rub someone the wrong way » veut dire irriter quelqu'un, souvent sans le vouloir.

questions.q: What does the idiom "sail close to the wind" mean?
o: To take a risky approach, close to breaking rules
To stay far from any danger
To sail a boat safely in calm water
questions.e: « Sail close to the wind » veut dire prendre un risque, flirter avec la limite autorisée.

questions.q: What does the idiom "set the record straight" mean?
o: To correct a misunderstanding by giving the true facts
questions.e: « Set the record straight » veut dire rétablir la vérité.

questions.q: What does the idiom "show your true colors" mean?
o: To hide your real personality successfully
To reveal your real character, often a negative one
questions.e: « Show your true colors » veut dire révéler sa vraie nature.

questions.q: What does the idiom "skeletons in the closet" mean?
o: Secret and often embarrassing facts about someone's past
questions.e: « Skeletons in the closet » désigne des secrets honteux du passé.

questions.q: What does the idiom "steal the limelight" mean?
o: To share attention fairly with others
To take all the attention away from others
questions.e: « Steal the limelight » veut dire attirer toute l'attention sur soi.

questions.q: What does the idiom "straight from the horse's mouth" mean?
o: A quote from an actual horse
Information obtained directly from the most reliable source
questions.e: « Straight from the horse's mouth » veut dire une information venant directement de la source la plus fiable.

questions.q: What does the idiom "take the bull by the horns" mean?
o: To ask someone else to solve a problem
To work on a farm with cattle
To confront a difficult situation directly and bravely
questions.e: « Take the bull by the horns » veut dire affronter directement une situation difficile.

questions.q: What does the idiom "the writing is on the wall" mean?
o: There is literal graffiti on a wall
There are clear signs that something bad is going to happen
questions.e: « The writing is on the wall » veut dire qu'il y a des signes clairs d'un problème à venir.

questions.q: What does the idiom "throw down the gauntlet" mean?
o: To drop a glove by accident
To challenge someone to a contest or confrontation
questions.e: « Throw down the gauntlet » veut dire lancer un défi à quelqu'un.

questions.q: What does the idiom "at loggerheads" mean?
o: In serious disagreement or conflict with someone
questions.e: « At loggerheads » veut dire être en désaccord profond avec quelqu'un.

questions.q: What does the idiom "in someone's good books" mean?
o: In someone's favour; approved of by them
questions.e: « In someone's good books » veut dire bénéficier de la faveur de quelqu'un.

questions.q: What does the idiom "burn the candle at both ends" mean?
o: To work or stay active for too long without enough rest
To light two candles for decoration
questions.e: « Burn the candle at both ends » veut dire s'épuiser en travaillant sans repos suffisant.

questions.q: What does the idiom "call it quits" mean?
o: To decide to stop doing something, often together
questions.e: « Call it quits » veut dire décider d'arrêter quelque chose.

questions.q: What does the idiom "get a foot in the door" mean?
o: To be completely excluded from an opportunity
To gain an initial opportunity that could lead to more
questions.e: « Get a foot in the door » veut dire obtenir une première opportunité.

questions.q: What does the idiom "go down in history" mean?
o: To be remembered as important by future generations
questions.e: « Go down in history » veut dire être retenu par l'histoire comme important.

questions.q: What does the idiom "have a bone to pick with someone" mean?
o: To avoid ever speaking to someone
To share a meal with someone
To want to discuss a disagreement with someone
questions.e: « Have a bone to pick with someone » veut dire avoir un différend à régler avec quelqu'un.

questions.q: What does the idiom "have the gift of the gab" mean?
o: To be a very skilled and persuasive talker
To write beautifully but not speak well
To be extremely shy and quiet
questions.e: « Have the gift of the gab » veut dire avoir un grand talent pour parler et convaincre.

questions.q: What does the idiom "hit rock bottom" mean?
o: To reach the lowest and worst point of a difficult situation
To reach the highest point of success
questions.e: « Hit rock bottom » veut dire atteindre le point le plus bas d'une situation difficile.

questions.q: What does the idiom "keep something under wraps" mean?
o: To keep something secret, not yet revealed
questions.e: « Keep something under wraps » veut dire garder quelque chose secret.

questions.q: What does the idiom "make a clean breast of something" mean?
o: To confess something fully and honestly
questions.e: « Make a clean breast of something » veut dire tout avouer honnêtement.

questions.q: What does the idiom "muddy the waters" mean?
o: To solve a complicated problem quickly
To make a situation more confusing or complicated
questions.e: « Muddy the waters » veut dire rendre une situation plus confuse.

questions.q: What does the idiom "put one's foot down" mean?
o: To firmly insist on something or refuse to allow it
To step forward confidently while walking
questions.e: « Put one's foot down » veut dire s'imposer fermement sur une décision.

questions.q: What does the idiom "rest on one's laurels" mean?
o: To fail completely at every task
To continue working hard despite success
To stop trying because of satisfaction with past success
questions.e: « Rest on one's laurels » veut dire se satisfaire de succès passés sans plus d'efforts.

questions.q: What does the idiom "ride on someone's coattails" mean?
o: To achieve success entirely through your own effort
To help someone else succeed generously
To literally hold onto someone's clothing
To benefit from someone else's success without earning it yourself
questions.e: « Ride on someone's coattails » veut dire profiter du succès de quelqu'un d'autre.

questions.q: What does the idiom "can't see the forest for the trees" mean?
o: To be so focused on small details that you miss the overall picture
To avoid looking at details at all
To understand the big picture perfectly
To get lost in an actual forest
questions.e: « Can't see the forest for the trees » veut dire se perdre dans les détails et manquer la vue d'ensemble.

questions.q: What does the idiom "shoot from the hip" mean?
o: To think very carefully before speaking
To speak or act quickly without careful thought
questions.e: « Shoot from the hip » veut dire parler ou agir sans réfléchir longuement.

questions.q: What does the idiom "sit on your hands" mean?
o: To physically sit on your own hands
To fail to act when action is needed
questions.e: « Sit on your hands » veut dire rester inactif alors qu'il faudrait agir.

questions.q: What does the idiom "stick to your guns" mean?
o: To use actual weapons in an argument
To avoid any kind of conflict
To maintain your position despite pressure to change
questions.e: « Stick to your guns » veut dire maintenir sa position malgré la pression.

questions.q: What does the idiom "swallow your pride" mean?
o: To refuse any form of compromise
To accept something humbling, despite personal pride
questions.e: « Swallow your pride » veut dire accepter quelque chose malgré sa fierté.

questions.q: What does the idiom "turn over a new leaf" mean?
o: To start behaving in a better, new way
To continue the same bad habits
To give up trying to improve
To rake fallen leaves in autumn
questions.e: « Turn over a new leaf » veut dire changer de comportement pour le mieux.

questions.q: What does the idiom "twist someone's arm" mean?
o: To refuse to ask someone for a favour
To let someone decide completely freely
To persuade someone to do something, sometimes with pressure
questions.e: « Twist someone's arm » veut dire persuader quelqu'un, parfois avec insistance.

questions.q: What does the idiom "walk on eggshells" mean?
o: To behave very carefully to avoid upsetting someone
To literally walk on broken eggs
To confront someone directly without caution
questions.e: « Walk on eggshells » veut dire se comporter avec grande prudence pour ne pas fâcher quelqu'un.

questions.q: What does the idiom "a stone's throw away" mean?
questions.e: « A stone's throw away » veut dire tout près.

questions.q: What does the idiom "beat someone to the punch" mean?
o: To arrive late to an event
To do something before someone else does it
To copy someone's idea after they succeed
questions.e: « Beat someone to the punch » veut dire faire quelque chose avant quelqu'un d'autre.

questions.q: What does the idiom "bend over backwards" mean?
o: To make a great effort to help someone
To do the minimum possible effort
To refuse to help at all
questions.e: « Bend over backwards » veut dire se donner beaucoup de mal pour aider quelqu'un.

questions.q: What does the idiom "bite the hand that feeds you" mean?
o: To help someone who helped you
To feed an animal by hand
To harm someone who has helped or supported you
questions.e: « Bite the hand that feeds you » veut dire nuire à quelqu'un qui vous a aidé.

questions.q: What does the idiom "blow something out of proportion" mean?
o: To accurately describe a small problem
To exaggerate the importance of something
questions.e: « Blow something out of proportion » veut dire exagérer l'importance d'un fait.

questions.q: What does the idiom "bury the hatchet" mean?
o: To end a disagreement and make peace
questions.e: « Bury the hatchet » veut dire faire la paix après un conflit.

questions.q: What does the idiom "by hook or by crook" mean?
o: By any means necessary, fair or not
questions.e: « By hook or by crook » veut dire par tous les moyens possibles.

questions.q: What does the idiom "caught red-handed" mean?
o: Caught in the act of doing something wrong
Arriving late to a crime scene
questions.e: « Caught red-handed » veut dire pris en flagrant délit.

questions.q: What does the idiom "chip on your shoulder" mean?
o: A persistent feeling of resentment about a past unfair treatment
A piece of food stuck on clothing
A physical injury to the shoulder
questions.e: « Chip on your shoulder » désigne un ressentiment persistant lié à une injustice passée.

questions.q: What does the idiom "clutch at straws" mean?
o: To give up immediately without trying
To try desperate, unlikely solutions when in a difficult situation
To calmly consider all realistic options
questions.e: « Clutch at straws » veut dire se raccrocher à des solutions désespérées.

questions.q: What does the idiom "come out of your shell" mean?
o: To become more withdrawn and shy
To literally emerge from an eggshell
To hide from a social event
To become less shy and more sociable
questions.e: « Come out of your shell » veut dire devenir moins timide.

questions.q: What does the idiom "cross the line" mean?
o: To behave in an unacceptable way, beyond what is appropriate
To stay exactly within acceptable limits
To avoid any kind of behaviour
questions.e: « Cross the line » veut dire dépasser les limites acceptables.

questions.q: What does the idiom "cut your losses" mean?
o: To stop doing something unprofitable before losing more
questions.e: « Cut your losses » veut dire arrêter une activité non rentable avant d'y perdre davantage.

questions.q: What does the idiom "dig your heels in" mean?
o: To stubbornly refuse to change your position
To dig a hole in the ground
To quickly agree with a new proposal
questions.e: « Dig your heels in » veut dire refuser obstinément de changer d'avis.

questions.q: What does the idiom "draw the line" mean?
o: To literally draw a line on paper
To allow any kind of behaviour
To set a firm limit on acceptable behaviour
questions.e: « Draw the line » veut dire fixer une limite claire.

questions.q: What does the idiom "drive a hard bargain" mean?
o: To refuse to negotiate at all
To accept the first offer immediately
To negotiate firmly to get the best possible deal
questions.e: « Drive a hard bargain » veut dire négocier fermement pour obtenir le meilleur accord.

questions.q: What does the idiom "fall on deaf ears" mean?
o: To be ignored, even though stated clearly
To be heard and acted upon immediately
questions.e: « Fall on deaf ears » veut dire être ignoré malgré un message clair.

questions.q: What does the idiom "fish out of water" mean?
o: Someone who feels awkward or out of place in a situation
A person who swims very well
Someone very comfortable in their environment
questions.e: « Fish out of water » désigne quelqu'un qui se sent mal à l'aise, hors de son élément.

questions.q: What does the idiom "get off scot-free" mean?
o: To avoid punishment or consequences entirely
questions.e: « Get off scot-free » veut dire échapper complètement à une punition.

questions.q: What does the idiom "go out on a limb" mean?
o: To follow the safest, most popular option
To avoid any kind of risk
To take a risk by saying or doing something unconventional
questions.e: « Go out on a limb » veut dire prendre un risque en sortant du consensus.

questions.q: What does the idiom "have your cake and eat it too" mean?
o: To choose only one reasonable option
To want two incompatible good things at the same time
questions.e: « Have your cake and eat it too » veut dire vouloir deux avantages incompatibles.

questions.q: What does the idiom "hold your horses" mean?
o: To act as fast as possible
To take care of real horses
To wait and not act too hastily
questions.e: « Hold your horses » veut dire patienter, ne pas agir trop vite.

questions.q: What does the idiom "hit the jackpot" mean?
o: To lose a large amount of money
To have great unexpected success or luck
To work very hard for small gains
questions.e: « Hit the jackpot » veut dire obtenir un succès inattendu et important.

questions.q: What does the idiom "ignorance is bliss" mean?
o: Not knowing about a problem can sometimes feel more comfortable
questions.e: Cette expression veut dire qu'on est parfois plus heureux en ignorant certaines choses.

questions.q: What does the idiom "jump through hoops" mean?
o: To literally jump through a circular object
To refuse to complete a complicated task
To achieve something with no effort at all
To go through many difficult steps to achieve something
questions.e: « Jump through hoops » veut dire devoir franchir de nombreuses étapes difficiles.

questions.q: What does the idiom "keep your cards close to your chest" mean?
o: To play cards in a group openly
To keep your plans or intentions secret
To reveal all your plans immediately
To give away all your resources
questions.e: « Keep your cards close to your chest » veut dire garder ses intentions secrètes.

questions.q: What does the idiom "kick the bucket" mean?
o: To die (an informal, sometimes humorous way of saying it)
questions.e: « Kick the bucket » est une façon familière de dire « mourir ».

questions.q: What does the idiom "know something like the back of your hand" mean?
o: To forget details about a subject
To know almost nothing about a topic
To study something for the first time
questions.e: « Know something like the back of your hand » veut dire connaître quelque chose parfaitement.

questions.q: What does the idiom "let the genie out of the bottle" mean?
o: To grant someone three wishes literally
To release a situation that cannot easily be reversed or controlled afterward
To prevent any change from happening
To fully control every outcome of a situation
questions.e: « Let the genie out of the bottle » veut dire déclencher une situation devenue incontrôlable.

questions.q: What does the idiom "make or break" mean?
o: A decision or event that will determine success or failure
A situation with no real consequences
A guaranteed success with no risk
questions.e: « Make or break » désigne un moment décisif pour la réussite ou l'échec.

questions.q: What does the idiom "no love lost" mean?
o: There is no affection or friendliness between two people
A romantic relationship has just started
There is strong, warm friendship between two people
questions.e: « No love lost » veut dire qu'il n'y a aucune affection entre deux personnes.

questions.q: What does the idiom "off the beaten path" mean?
o: Along the most popular tourist route
Unusual, away from the common or popular route
questions.e: « Off the beaten path » veut dire inhabituel, loin des sentiers battus.

questions.q: What does the idiom "on the same wavelength" mean?
o: Listening to the same radio station only
Thinking in a similar way and understanding each other well
Unable to communicate with each other
questions.e: « On the same wavelength » veut dire penser de la même façon, bien se comprendre.

questions.q: What does the idiom "out of your depth" mean?
o: Completely confident and capable in a situation
In a situation beyond your knowledge or ability to handle
An expert in a particular subject
questions.e: « Out of your depth » veut dire dans une situation qui dépasse ses compétences.

questions.q: What does the idiom "play your cards right" mean?
o: To act wisely to achieve a good result
To act carelessly without any strategy
To refuse to take any action
To cheat during a card game
questions.e: « Play your cards right » veut dire agir intelligemment pour obtenir un bon résultat.

questions.q: What does the idiom "preaching to the choir" mean?
o: Trying to convince people who already agree with you
Giving a religious sermon in a church only
questions.e: « Preaching to the choir » veut dire essayer de convaincre des gens déjà convaincus.

questions.q: What does the idiom "pull out all the stops" mean?
o: To make every possible effort to succeed
To make the minimum possible effort
To refuse to try at all
questions.e: « Pull out all the stops » veut dire faire tous les efforts possibles.

questions.q: What does the idiom "put a damper on something" mean?
o: To make an event more exciting
To make an event or situation less enjoyable
To end an event early with celebration
To improve the mood of a situation
questions.e: « Put a damper on something » veut dire gâcher l'ambiance d'un événement.

questions.q: What does the idiom "rock the boat" mean?
o: To actually shake a boat on water
To disturb a stable situation, often causing problems
To keep a stable situation calm and unchanged
questions.e: « Rock the boat » veut dire perturber une situation stable.

questions.q: What does the idiom "run-of-the-mill" mean?
questions.e: « Run-of-the-mill » veut dire ordinaire, sans particularité.

questions.q: What does the idiom "sell like hotcakes" mean?
o: To be given away for free
To sell very quickly and in large quantities
questions.e: « Sell like hotcakes » veut dire se vendre très rapidement.

questions.q: What does the idiom "sink or swim" mean?
o: To avoid any kind of challenge
To succeed without any effort required
To either succeed through your own effort or fail completely
questions.e: « Sink or swim » veut dire devoir réussir seul, sans aide extérieure, ou échouer.

questions.q: What does the idiom "spread yourself too thin" mean?
o: To finish all your tasks early
To focus on only one task carefully
To take on too many tasks or commitments at once
questions.e: « Spread yourself too thin » veut dire s'engager dans trop de choses à la fois.

questions.q: What does the idiom "the lion's share" mean?
questions.e: « The lion's share » désigne la plus grande partie de quelque chose.

questions.q: What does the idiom "the pot calling the kettle black" mean?
o: Criticising someone for a fault that you also have yourself
Cooking a meal in the kitchen
questions.e: « The pot calling the kettle black » veut dire critiquer un défaut que l'on possède soi-même.
